images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of the SpatialArena benchmark.(a) SpatialArena against existing geometry benchmarks along six axes, each normalized by its largest value (sequence length in log frames); E3D-Bench dataset counts are a lower bound. (b) Datasets, models, and longest sequence of each benchmark. (c) Score of eight leading models on each dataset;†\daggermarks datasets excluded from the ranking. No model leads on every dataset. (d) Evaluated models by family. (e) Scenes of our Spatial Arena dataset, which feeds all five tasks.

Figure 3:Overview of the Spatial Arena dataset.Top left:RGB images with sparse LiDAR depth, dense depth rendered from the 3DGS[47]reconstruction, for forward- and upward-looking cameras indoors and outdoors; the dense depth fills the gaps between LiDAR returns, and masked regions such as the sky stay invalid.Right and bottom left:LiDAR maps of indoor and outdoor scenes
with camera trajectories drawn as colored curves.Bottom right:a reconstructed 3DGS scene (RGB, depth, and normal) with its trajectory.
Figure 4:MonoDepth score vs. paper date. Lines: per-family least-squares fits; legend: slope and score. Other tasks inFigs.9and10.
Figure 5:MonoDepth predictions on AerialMetric, aligned and colored on the ground-truth scale (black: masked region); each tag gives the frame’s AbsRel as a fraction.

Figure 6:MVRecon reconstructionson ETH3D and Tanks&Temples, aligned to the ground truth as in evaluation. Ground-truth cameras are drawn in black and predicted cameras in purple. The tag on each reconstruction gives its F-score (τ=25\tau=25cm), Acc, and Comp (in m).

Figure 7:What makes Spatial Arena difficult.(a) Images from 14 scenes, taken by the front camera (upright views along the walking direction) and the two side cameras (rolled views looking up and sideways): dim museum halls with specular floors, a tiled underground platform, close-ups of floors and signs, graffiti, foliage, stairs, and facades seen from below. (b) Depth range within one image (d95/d5d_{95}/d_{5}of the valid ground truth; box: quartiles, whiskers: 10th and 90th percentiles) on the 1,688 Spatial Arena MonoDepth images and a sample of the real public MonoDepth datasets (Marigold suite without ETH3D). (c) Absolute camera roll of the same images, from the ground-truth poses (worldzzis vertical): the front camera is nearly upright (median5∘5^{\circ}), whereas the side cameras are rolled by a median of50∘50^{\circ}. (d) Mean MonoDepth AbsRel of four models in bins of camera roll.
Figure 9:Task score against paper date(first arXiv version) for VideoDepth and MVRecon, as inFig.4. Circles are thergbtrack; triangles mark thergbc([+C]) andrgbd([+D]) tracks.
Figure 11:MonoDepth predictionson one frame of Spring and of Spatial Arena, shown as inFig.5.†Excluded from the ranking.

Figure 12:MonoDepth predictions of the depth specialistson two iBims-1 frames, shown as inFig.5. On the simple room (a), all models are within 0.016–0.034 AbsRel, and MoGe-2 and MoGe-3 are best. On the cluttered frame (b), the thin leaves and railings raise every error by a factor of 2.5–4.6; MoGe-3 is again best (0.069) and Depth Pro worst (0.103).

Figure 13:MonoDepth predictions and AbsRel error maps on two Spatial Arena frames.Depth maps share the color scale of the ground truth; error maps run from 0 (blue) to≥\geq0.25 (red), and grey marks pixels without valid depth. In the garden (a, b), MoGe-2 is most accurate (0.186) and MoGe-3 least (0.271), with its largest errors on the pergola beams; VGGT-Ω\Omegadoes not separate the beams from the background (inset). On the canal (c, d), MoGe-3 is most accurate (0.193) and Depth Pro least (0.344), with large errors over most of the frame; MoGe-2 and MoGe-3 err in bands on the near surface at the top.

Figure 14:MonoDepth predictions of the commercial VLMson a Spatial Arena frame (CambridgeRalishLibrary), next to VGGT and VGGT-Ω\Omega, shown as inFig.5. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra return nearly flat depth (AbsRel 0.399 and 0.392); Gemini 4 Argon recovers the layout (0.153) and stays behind VGGT-Ω\Omega(0.112). The VLM maps are interpolated from a16×1616{\times}16query grid (Sec.D.3.2) and cannot represent fine structure.

Figure 15:MonoDepth predictions of the VLMson a HAMMER and an NYUv2 frame, shown as inFig.5. All VLMs recover the layout of the scene. The commercial VLMs answer a16×1616{\times}16grid of points (Sec.D.3.2), so their interpolated maps cannot resolve object boundaries by construction. Gemini 4 Argon is best on HAMMER (0.053) and DepthLM on NYUv2 (0.056); Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, and DepthVLM have errors of 0.092–0.120 on both frames.

Figure 16:VideoDepth predictions on public sequences, one frame each, shown as inFig.5. On the dynamic scenes of Bonn (a) and DyCheck (b), the feed-forward 3D/4D models have the lowest errors (DA3-NGL 0.032 and VGGT-Ω\Omega0.038 on Bonn; VGGT-Ω\Omega0.026 andπ3\pi^{3}-X 0.053 on DyCheck), below those of the video depth models DVD, ChronoDepth, and DepthCrafter (0.051–0.109).

Figure 17:VideoDepth predictions on Spatial Arena sequences, shown as inFig.16. In the library corridor (a), Déjà View andπ3\pi^{3}-X are best (0.044), while ChronoDepth misses the depth of the far opening (0.171). On the close-up of a nearly planar surface in the museum (b), every model fails to some degree (0.117–0.375):π3\pi^{3}-X and AMB3R are best, and VGGT-Ω\Omega(0.287) and DA3-NGL (0.375) are worst.

Figure 18:MVRecon reconstructions on a HiRoom scene, shown as inFig.6, in color (a) and colored by each point’s distance to the ground truth (b). DA3-NGL (F-score 0.943), VGGT-Ω\Omega(0.928), and VGGT (0.875) reconstruct the room almost exactly, whereas the errors of OmniVGGT (0.293) and Pow3R (0.141) spread over whole walls.

Figure 19:MVRecon failure cases on Spatial Arena, shown as inFig.6. On these large scenes, no model exceeds an F-score of 0.35 atτ=25\tau=25cm: the best areπ3\pi^{3}-X in the garden (a, 0.349) and VGGT-Ω\Omegain the museum (b, 0.159).

Figure 20:A third MVRecon failure case on Spatial Arena, shown as inFig.19. Most models recover a recognizable shape of the roof, but at the wrong scale and position, so few points fall withinτ=5\tau=5cm; the best F-score is 0.124 (VGGT-Ω\Omega).

Figure 22:SfM on two public scenes.Each panel shows an input image, the predicted cameras afterSim⁡(3)\mathrm{Sim}(3)alignment (one color per model, ground truth in dark gray), and the fraction of image pairs whose pose errormax⁡(eR,et)\max(e^{R},e^{t})is below each threshold, with the AUC at5∘5^{\circ},10∘10^{\circ}, and30∘30^{\circ}in the legend. On the object-centric DTU scene (a), all models but MapAnything reach an AUC@5∘5^{\circ}of 0.73–0.88 (VGGT best, 0.883); MapAnything (0.219) shifts the cameras of the outer rings. On the unordered internet photos of IMC (b), VGGT-Ω\Omegais best (0.484), followed by Déjà View (0.435) and DA3-NGL (0.428), whereas AMB3R (0.160) leaves about a third of the pairs above30∘30^{\circ}.

Figure 23:SfM on a Spatial Arena scene(Dugald Stewart Monument, 300 images), shown as inFig.22, with the cameras of each model in a separate panel. All models recover the shape of the loop, but their cameras scatter around it, and the AUC@5∘5^{\circ}is far below that on the public scenes: Déjà View is best (0.230), followed by VGGT-Ω\Omega(0.104); VGGT, DA3-NGL, andπ3\pi^{3}-X stay below 0.05, and the cameras of MapAnything (0.005) leave the loop.

Figure 24:SfM on a second Spatial Arena scene(St Giles’ Cathedral statue, 300 images), shown as inFig.23. Déjà View (AUC@5∘5^{\circ}0.424) and VGGT-Ω\Omega(0.233) follow the repeated loops around the statue; DA3-NGL and VGGT (0.128 and 0.121) add spurious jumps across the loop, and the cameras of OmniVGGT (0.014) and MapAnything (0.002) scatter over its inside.
